description:
1. Description:
The bird is mostly gray in color. The top of its head is black and the tip of its tail is also black. Underneath the tail it has an orange/reddish spot that is quite noticeable. It also has 2 very skinny legs with 3 front facing claws and 1 back facing claw. 

2. Habitat: 
I took the picture of this bird in front of the education building near the library on USF Tampa's campus. Nearby there are many trees and other birds are spotted all of the time flying around that area of campus. It was a shady/gloomy day after raining for a bit that morning and the bird was just at the front of the education building standing there. 

3. Reference:
https://www.audubon.org/field-guide/bird/gray-catbird. According to the Audubon field guide on the Gray Catbird, the pictures on the website match the bird I pictured exactly. There is a distinct orange patch under its tail and it does a lot of foraging on the ground, most likely the reason I was able to picture it here on the ground.
